text:
Passive movements are movements of a body part produced by an external force (such as a therapist, machine, or gravity) rather than by the person's own muscle contraction. They are used in assessment (e.g., checking joint range of motion) and in treatment (e.g., preventing stiffness when a patient cannot move actively). The note claiming they are performed against resistance and stretch the joint at end range describes something more like a passive stretch, not passive movement generally.
CONFIDENCE: 95
